why: The last two of dotenv's ten findings are `tests/test-parse.js:88` and `tests/test-parse-multiline.js:62`, and both are `{ SERVER: 'localhost', PASSWORD: 'password', DB: 'tests' }` -- the expected payload of a parser test. `password` is the word the key already says; as a VALUE it announces itself as a stand-in, the same way `changeme` and `your-...` already do in PLACEHOLDER_FORTE. THIS IS NOT "any line in a test file", and that boundary is the whole point of the case: the fail side is the same fixture, the same key and the same test, with a value that announces NOTHING -- and a credential inside a fixture is still a credential, so the rule has to go on catching it. A word passphrase and not a high-entropy body, on purpose: what decides the exemption is the value BEING the word the key says, never its entropy, and a fixture does not need to look leaked to every other scanner that reads this repository. The alternative is anchored to the END of the span, so it only ever fires when the value IS the word and nothing else. Whoever exempts on the word appearing ANYWHERE in the span exempts the key too, and every `password: '...'` in the repository with it.
